facts.statement: The genus was discovered in Italy and originally described by Simonelli as a crocodyliform related to Dakosaurus.
facts.quote: It was discovered in Italy, and described by Simonelli, originally believing it to be a metriorhynchid crocodyliform similar to Dakosaurus.

facts.statement: Sirotti later re-examined the type specimen and concluded that Capellineosuchus was a junior synonym of Mosasaurus hoffmannii.
facts.quote: However, after re-examining the type specimen, Sirotti concluded that it was a junior synonym of Mosasaurus hoffmannii.

facts.statement: A 2014 study determined that the genus is distinct from Mosasaurus hoffmannii.
facts.quote: A 2014 paper found the genus to be distinct from M. hoffmannii.

facts.statement: The name Capellineosuchus is a misspelling created by Romer.
facts.quote: Capellineosuchus is a misspelling by Romer.

facts.statement: Capelliniosuchus is an extinct genus of mosasaur.
facts.quote: Capelliniosuchus is an extinct genus of mosasaur.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group as Metriorhynchidae.
Fossils of this animal date to the Late Cretaceous period.
